function.name: read_file
function.description: Read the complete contents of a file as text. DEPRECATED: Use read_text_file instead.

tail.description: If provided, returns only the last N lines of the file

head.description: If provided, returns only the first N lines of the file

function.name: read_text_file
function.description: Read the complete contents of a file from the file system as text. Handles various text encodings and provides detailed error messages if the file cannot be read. Use this tool when you need to examine the contents of a single file. Use the 'head' parameter to read only the first N lines of a file, or the 'tail' parameter to read only the last N lines of a file. Operates on the file as text regardless of extension. Only works within allowed directories.

tail.description: If provided, returns only the last N lines of the file

head.description: If provided, returns only the first N lines of the file

function.name: read_media_file
function.description: Read a file and return it as a base64-encoded content block with its MIME type. Image and audio files are returned as image/audio content; any other file type is returned as an embedded resource. Only works within allowed directories.

function.name: read_multiple_files
function.description: Read the contents of multiple files simultaneously. This is more efficient than reading files one by one when you need to analyze or compare multiple files. Each file's content is returned with its path as a reference. Failed reads for individual files won't stop the entire operation. Only works within allowed directories.

paths.description: Array of file paths to read. Each path must be a string pointing to a valid file within allowed directories.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a new file or completely overwrite an existing file with new content. Use with caution as it will overwrite existing files without warning. Handles text content with proper encoding. Only works within allowed directories.

function.name: edit_file
function.description: Make line-based edits to a text file. Each edit replaces exact line sequences with new content. Returns a git-style diff showing the changes made. Only works within allowed directories.

oldText.description: Text to search for - must match exactly

dryRun.description: Preview changes using git-style diff format

function.name: create_directory
function.description: Create a new directory or ensure a directory exists. Can create multiple nested directories in one operation. If the directory already exists, this operation will succeed silently. Perfect for setting up directory structures for projects or ensuring required paths exist. Only works within allowed directories.

function.name: list_directory
function.description: Get a detailed listing of all files and directories in a specified path. Results clearly distinguish between files and directories with [FILE] and [DIR] prefixes. This tool is essential for understanding directory structure and finding specific files within a directory. Only works within allowed directories.

function.name: list_directory_with_sizes
function.description: Get a detailed listing of all files and directories in a specified path, including sizes. Results clearly distinguish between files and directories with [FILE] and [DIR] prefixes. This tool is useful for understanding directory structure and finding specific files within a directory. Only works within allowed directories.

sortBy.description: Sort entries by name or size

function.name: directory_tree
function.description: Get a recursive tree view of files and directories as a JSON structure. Each entry includes 'name', 'type' (file/directory), and 'children' for directories. Files have no children array, while directories always have a children array (which may be empty). The output is formatted with 2-space indentation for readability. Only works within allowed directories.

function.name: move_file
function.description: Move or rename files and directories. Can move files between directories and rename them in a single operation. If the destination exists, the operation will fail. Works across different directories and can be used for simple renaming within the same directory. Both source and destination must be within allowed directories.

function.name: search_files
function.description: Recursively search for files and directories matching a pattern. The patterns should be glob-style patterns that match paths relative to the working directory. Use pattern like '*.ext' to match files in current directory, and '**/*.ext' to match files in all subdirectories. Returns full paths to all matching items. Great for finding files when you don't know their exact location. Only searches within allowed directories.

function.name: get_file_info
function.description: Retrieve detailed metadata about a file or directory. Returns comprehensive information including size, creation time, last modified time, permissions, and type. This tool is perfect for understanding file characteristics without reading the actual content. Only works within allowed directories.

function.name: list_allowed_directories
function.description: Returns the list of directories that this server is allowed to access. Subdirectories within these allowed directories are also accessible. Use this to understand which directories and their nested paths are available before trying to access files.

function.name: ironclad_preprocess
function.description: Run a user message through the full ironclad defense pipeline: PromptGuard injection detection → BERT-NER/regex PII redaction → RAG-augmented LLM rewrite. Returns the sanitised text, whether it was modified, and whether PromptGuard flagged it as a prompt injection. Use this before forwarding untrusted user input to a downstream model.

text.description: The raw user message to sanitise.

enable_rewriting.description: Whether to rewrite the message (default true).

config.description: Optional per-call overrides of the ironclad-api pipeline config. Any field omitted falls back to the server-wide ironclad_config.json / CLI-flag default.

passthrough.description: Return query unchanged when classified benign

pii_passthrough.description: Offload PII handling to the rewriter LLM instead of the BERT NER model

ironclad_model.description: Rewriter model name (e.g. qwen3:4b for Ollama, or a HuggingFace repo ID)

function.name: ironclad_guard
function.description: Classify a text string for prompt injection using ironclad's PromptGuard model. Returns whether the text is considered a prompt injection attempt.

text.description: The user message or prompt to classify.

config.description: Optional per-call overrides of the ironclad-api pipeline config. Any field omitted falls back to the server-wide ironclad_config.json / CLI-flag default.

passthrough.description: Return query unchanged when classified benign

pii_passthrough.description: Offload PII handling to the rewriter LLM instead of the BERT NER model

ironclad_model.description: Rewriter model name (e.g. qwen3:4b for Ollama, or a HuggingFace repo ID)

function.name: ironclad_shieldstral
function.description: Classify a text string for general harmful content using ironclad's Shieldstral model (or a compatible swappable guard model). Unlike ironclad_guard (PromptGuard, jailbreak/injection only), this detects harmful content more broadly and can adjust its harm taxonomy in-context. Returns whether the text is considered harmful.

text.description: The user message or prompt to classify.

shieldstral_model.description: HF repo ID for the guard model (default: models.shieldstral from config, mistralai/Shieldstral-1.0-3B unless set). Swappable across meta-llama/Llama-Guard-4-12B, openai/gpt-oss-safeguard-20b, meta-llama/Llama-Guard-3-11B-Vision, meta-llama/Llama-Guard-3-8B.

image_b64.description: Base64-encoded image (PNG or JPEG) for genuine multimodal classification. Only the shieldstral family (the default model) actually inspects it — llama_guard-family models (including the nominally-vision meta-llama/Llama-Guard-3-11B-Vision) ignore it.

config.description: Optional per-call overrides of the ironclad-api pipeline config. Any field omitted falls back to the server-wide ironclad_config.json / CLI-flag default.

passthrough.description: Return query unchanged when classified benign

pii_passthrough.description: Offload PII handling to the rewriter LLM instead of the BERT NER model

ironclad_model.description: Rewriter model name (e.g. qwen3:4b for Ollama, or a HuggingFace repo ID)

function.name: ironclad_redact
function.description: Redact PII / PHI entities from text using ironclad's BERT NER model (models.pii) with a regex fallback. Sensitive entities (names, dates, SSNs, emails, medical record numbers, etc.) are replaced with placeholder tokens like [NAME], [DATE], [SSN], [EMAIL], [MEDICAL_ID].

text.description: Text that may contain PII or PHI to redact.

config.description: Optional per-call overrides of the ironclad-api pipeline config. Any field omitted falls back to the server-wide ironclad_config.json / CLI-flag default.

passthrough.description: Return query unchanged when classified benign

pii_passthrough.description: Offload PII handling to the rewriter LLM instead of the BERT NER model

ironclad_model.description: Rewriter model name (e.g. qwen3:4b for Ollama, or a HuggingFace repo ID)

function.name: ironclad_rewrite
function.description: Sanitise a user message through ironclad's RAG-augmented rewrite pipeline. The model neutralises prompt-injection phrasing, adversarial instructions, and jailbreak attempts while preserving the original intent. Returns the rewritten text and a flag indicating whether any change was made.

config.description: Optional per-call overrides of the ironclad-api pipeline config. Any field omitted falls back to the server-wide ironclad_config.json / CLI-flag default.

passthrough.description: Return query unchanged when classified benign

pii_passthrough.description: Offload PII handling to the rewriter LLM instead of the BERT NER model

ironclad_model.description: Rewriter model name (e.g. qwen3:4b for Ollama, or a HuggingFace repo ID)

function.name: ironclad_rag_query
function.description: Retrieve the top-k most relevant document chunks from the ironclad golden vector store for a given query. Returns a list of plain-text chunks ordered by descending relevance. Use this to inject RAG context into a prompt before sending it to a downstream LLM.

text.description: Query string to embed and search against the vector store.

k.description: Number of document chunks to retrieve. Defaults to the server-configured top_k.

function.name: ironclad_rag_query_scored
function.description: Like ironclad_rag_query but returns each chunk together with a relevance score so callers can apply a threshold. NOTE: the score is a rank-based proxy (1.0 for the top result, decreasing linearly to the last), not a true cosine similarity — no scored backend endpoint exists yet. Useful for relative ranking / cutting off low-relevance tail results, not for comparing scores across different queries. Result is a JSON array of {"text": str, "score": float} objects.

text.description: Query string to embed and search against the vector store.

k.description: Number of document chunks to retrieve.

min_score.description: Optional minimum score (0-1, rank-based proxy — see tool description). Chunks below this threshold are omitted.

function.name: ironclad_rag_build
function.description: Build (or rebuild) the ironclad golden vector store from a list of plain-text documents. Useful for seeding the RAG index from agent-collected content without using ironclad-make-db. For very large datasets (>10k docs) prefer the CLI tool instead.

texts.description: List of plain-text document strings to index.

overwrite.description: Remove and rebuild if the DB already exists (default true).

function.name: ironclad_rag_inspect
function.description: Inspect the current ironclad vector store: returns the number of indexed vectors and optional sample query results with scores. Safe to call even if the DB has not been built yet.

sample_queries.description: Queries to run against the DB. Omit for built-in defaults. Pass [] to skip queries and return only the vector count.

function.name: ironclad_ingest_preview
function.description: List files under a server-side directory that would be ingested, given optional include/exclude glob filters — no extraction happens, no dataset is written. Use this to tune filter patterns before running ironclad_ingest_directory on a potentially large directory.

include.description: Comma-separated glob pattern(s) to include (e.g. "*.pdf,*.docx"). Defaults to common document extensions.

exclude.description: Comma-separated glob pattern(s) to exclude, even if matched by include (e.g. "*/archive/*,*draft*").

function.name: ironclad_ingest_file
function.description: Extract text from a single server-side file synchronously — no dataset is written. Use this to inspect or quote one document without running a whole-directory batch job.

file_path.description: Server-side path to the file to extract.

backend.description: Extraction backend: classical (default, unstructured, no model download) or vlm-ocr (configurable OCR model, higher fidelity on scans/tables/complex layouts).

ocr_model.description: HF repo ID for backend=vlm-ocr (default: models.ocr from the server's config, allenai/olmOCR-2-7B-1025 unless set).

ocr_batch_size.description: Page images per OCR chunk for backend=vlm-ocr (default: ingest.ocr_batch_size from the server's config, 4 unless set).

function.name: ironclad_ingest_directory
function.description: Ingest every matching file under a server-side directory into a single HF dataset, saved server-side and directly consumable by ironclad-preprocess/ironclad-make-db via --dataset-path. Runs as a background job on the server — returns a job_id immediately; poll with ironclad_ingest_status.

output_path.description: Server-side path to save the resulting HF dataset.

ocr_model.description: HF repo ID for backend=vlm-ocr (default: models.ocr from the server's config, allenai/olmOCR-2-7B-1025 unless set).

ocr_batch_size.description: Page images per OCR chunk for backend=vlm-ocr (default: ingest.ocr_batch_size from the server's config, 4 unless set).

function.name: ironclad_ingest_status
function.description: Poll the status of a job started by ironclad_ingest_directory: queued/running/done/error, plus processed/total file counts.

function.name: ironclad_classify_refusal
function.description: Classify a single model response as a refusal or not using ironclad's keyword-based StringClassifier (JailbreakBench heuristic). Fast, no GPU required. Useful for post-processing responses after a preprocess run.

function.name: ironclad_classify_refusal_batch
function.description: Classify a list of model responses as refusals or not in a single call. Uses ironclad's keyword-based StringClassifier (JailbreakBench heuristic). Returns one boolean per input response.

texts.description: List of model responses to classify.

function.name: ironclad_classify_refusal_llm
function.description: Classify a single (prompt, response) pair as a refusal using an LLM judge (Llama3RefusalJudge, default meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct). Higher accuracy than ironclad_classify_refusal's keyword heuristic, at the cost of a model load and GPU/MPS inference on the server.

judge_model.description: HF repo ID for the judge model (default: models.judge from the server's config, meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct unless set).

function.name: ironclad_classify_refusal_llm_batch
function.description: Classify a batch of (prompt, response) pairs as refusals in one call using an LLM judge. Same model as ironclad_classify_refusal_llm.

responses.description: Model responses to classify, aligned 1:1 with prompts.

judge_model.description: HF repo ID for the judge model (default: models.judge from the server's config, meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct unless set).

function.name: ironclad_classify_harmful
function.description: Classify a single (prompt, response) pair for harmfulness using Llama Guard (LlamaGuardClassifier, default meta-llama/Llama-Guard-3-8B) — its native user/assistant moderation format, not a generic refusal judge.

harmguard_model.description: HF repo ID for the harmfulness judge (default: models.harmguard from the server's config, meta-llama/Llama-Guard-3-8B unless set).

function.name: ironclad_classify_harmful_batch
function.description: Classify a batch of (prompt, response) pairs for harmfulness in one call using Llama Guard. Same model as ironclad_classify_harmful.

responses.description: Model responses to classify, aligned 1:1 with prompts.

harmguard_model.description: HF repo ID for the harmfulness judge (default: models.harmguard from the server's config, meta-llama/Llama-Guard-3-8B unless set).

function.name: create_entities
function.description: Create multiple new entities in the knowledge graph

observations.description: An array of observation contents associated with the entity

function.name: create_relations
function.description: Create multiple new relations between entities in the knowledge graph. Relations should be in active voice

from.description: The name of the entity where the relation starts

to.description: The name of the entity where the relation ends

function.name: add_observations
function.description: Add new observations to existing entities in the knowledge graph

entityName.description: The name of the entity to add the observations to

contents.description: An array of observation contents to add

function.name: delete_entities
function.description: Delete multiple entities and their associated relations from the knowledge graph

entityNames.description: An array of entity names to delete

function.name: delete_observations
function.description: Delete specific observations from entities in the knowledge graph

entityName.description: The name of the entity containing the observations

observations.description: An array of observations to delete

function.name: delete_relations
function.description: Delete multiple relations from the knowledge graph

from.description: The name of the entity where the relation starts

to.description: The name of the entity where the relation ends

relations.description: An array of relations to delete

function.name: read_graph
function.description: Read the entire knowledge graph

function.name: search_nodes
function.description: Search for nodes in the knowledge graph based on a query

query.description: The search query to match against entity names, types, and observation content

function.name: open_nodes
function.description: Open specific nodes in the knowledge graph by their names

names.description: An array of entity names to retrieve

function.name: chroma_list_collections
function.description:
List all collection names in the Chroma database with pagination support.
    
    Args:
        limit: Optional maximum number of collections to return
        offset: Optional number of collections to skip before returning results
    
    Returns:
        List of collection names or ["__NO_COLLECTIONS_FOUND__"] if database is empty

function.name: chroma_create_collection
function.description:
Create a new Chroma collection with configurable HNSW parameters.
    
    Args:
        collection_name: Name of the collection to create
        embedding_function_name: Name of the embedding function to use. Options: 'default', 'cohere', 'openai', 'jina', 'voyageai', 'ollama', 'roboflow'
        metadata: Optional metadata dict to add to the collection

function.name: chroma_peek_collection
function.description:
Peek at documents in a Chroma collection.
    
    Args:
        collection_name: Name of the collection to peek into
        limit: Number of documents to peek at

function.name: chroma_get_collection_info
function.description:
Get information about a Chroma collection.
    
    Args:
        collection_name: Name of the collection to get info about

function.name: chroma_get_collection_count
function.description:
Get the number of documents in a Chroma collection.
    
    Args:
        collection_name: Name of the collection to count

function.name: chroma_modify_collection
function.description:
Modify a Chroma collection's name or metadata.
    
    Args:
        collection_name: Name of the collection to modify
        new_name: Optional new name for the collection
        new_metadata: Optional new metadata for the collection

function.name: chroma_fork_collection
function.description:
Fork a Chroma collection.
    
    Args:
        collection_name: Name of the collection to fork
        new_collection_name: Name of the new collection to create
        metadata: Optional metadata dict to add to the new collection

function.name: chroma_delete_collection
function.description:
Delete a Chroma collection.
    
    Args:
        collection_name: Name of the collection to delete

function.name: chroma_add_documents
function.description:
Add documents to a Chroma collection.
    
    Args:
        collection_name: Name of the collection to add documents to
        documents: List of text documents to add
        ids: List of IDs for the documents (required)
        metadatas: Optional list of metadata dictionaries for each document

function.name: chroma_query_documents
chroma_get_documents
chroma_update_documents
function.description:
Update documents in a Chroma collection.

    Args:
        collection_name: Name of the collection to update documents in
        ids: List of document IDs to update (required)
        embeddings: Optional list of new embeddings for the documents.
                    Must match length of ids if provided.
        metadatas: Optional list of new metadata dictionaries for the documents.
                   Must match length of ids if provided.
        documents: Optional list of new text documents.
                   Must match length of ids if provided.

    Returns:
        A confirmation message indicating the number of documents updated.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If 'ids' is empty or if none of 'embeddings', 'metadatas',
                    or 'documents' are provided, or if the length of provided
                    update lists does not match the length of 'ids'.
        Exception: If the collection does not exist or if the update operation fails.

function.name: chroma_delete_documents
function.description:
Delete documents from a Chroma collection.

    Args:
        collection_name: Name of the collection to delete documents from
        ids: List of document IDs to delete

    Returns:
        A confirmation message indicating the number of documents deleted.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If 'ids' is empty
        Exception: If the collection does not exist or if the delete operation fails.
